Works with

Rugged tablet for Infraspeak Next

Infraspeak is a maintenance and facilities management platform from Infraspeak S.A., a company incorporated in Portugal with its registered office in Porto (its general terms, in force since 15 September 2026, give company number 513 468 480). The vendor describes it as a platform that uses AI and predictive intelligence to connect a facilities management ecosystem in one place, and its site lists facility management, retail, hospitality, healthcare, education, HVAC, lifts and electrical maintenance among the sectors it serves. The manager's side runs in a web browser and in the Infraspeak Manager app; the people doing the work use Infraspeak Next, the technician app on Google Play and the App Store.

On site, Infraspeak Next is where a technician opens, approves, pauses and closes work orders, creates work orders by location by scanning a QR code, a barcode or an NFC tag, checks the work order list and its details, adds and views documents, exchanges messages with the team inside a work order, and works offline. Infraspeak's academy documents NFC tags assigned to equipment, users and locations, with one tag per item, and a sign-in by holding the device to a tag. That work happens in plant rooms, risers, kitchens and car parks, which is where a consumer tablet with an exposed screen and a small battery struggles.

This page sets out what Infraspeak publishes about the device the Next app needs, matches those figures to the Tuga range, and says which device fits and which does not. Every Tuga figure comes from our catalogue; every Infraspeak figure comes from the vendor's own pages, linked beside it. We have not tested the app on these devices and do not claim Infraspeak has, so start with one unit on a trial before buying for a team.

Requirements

What Infraspeak (Infraspeak Next app) needs from a device

Each item below comes from Infraspeak S.A.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 10 or later at minimum; Android 13 or later recommended

    The Infraspeak Academy article How to download the Infraspeak Next app on your device (undated; checked 25 October 2026) lists minimum device requirements of Android phones and tablets with Android 10 or later versions, and recommended requirements of Android phones and tablets with Android 13 or later versions. The same article lists iPhones and iPads with iOS 16 or later for Apple devices. The Google Play listing (Infraspeak Next, package com.infraspeak.one, developer Infraspeak S.A., 10,000 or more downloads when checked) did not display its own Requires Android figure in our check, so the academy figures are the ones to plan on. Source: academy.infraspeak.com

  • 4GB of RAM at minimum; 6GB or more recommended

    The same academy article gives 4 GB of RAM or superior as the minimum and 6 GB of RAM or superior as the recommended figure. Source: academy.infraspeak.com

  • 32GB of storage or more

    The academy article lists 32 GB of Storage or superior under both the minimum and the recommended requirements. Source: academy.infraspeak.com

  • Camera and NFC sensor, optional but needed for scanning tags, QR codes and barcodes

    The academy article lists Camera and NFC Sensor with a footnote: these characteristics aren't mandatory but they will allow you to scan NFC Tags, QR Codes and Barcodes within the app. The Google Play description for Infraspeak Next says users can create work orders by location, with QR or barcode and with NFC tags. A separate academy article on assigning NFC tags to a location says the technician must swipe the tag near the NFC reader on the mobile device, and that there can only be one NFC tag for an equipment, user or location. Source: academy.infraspeak.com

  • Offline working, with limits the vendor documents

    The Google Play description lists Work offline among the app's features. The academy article Infraspeak Next offline capabilities says all actions that are done offline are stored on the device until the user regains an internet or mobile network connection with the app open, after which the app syncs the changes; that planned job orders must be started while online, only after starting them will the user be able to operate offline; and that the app must be fully synchronised to be able to find assets while offline. The article's detailed list of offline features is published as an image, so check it against your own workflow. Source: academy.infraspeak.com

  • Sign in by email and password, or by NFC tag

    The academy's log in or log off article gives two routes: enter the registered email and password, or open the app and hold the device near the NFC tag linked to the user's account. The article gives no date. Source: academy.infraspeak.com

  • No Windows app for technicians; the manager's interface runs in a browser

    The Infraspeak site lists the Infraspeak Next and Infraspeak Manager apps for the App Store and Google Play, and describes the manager's features as a web interface. Neither the site nor the academy article names a Windows requirement or a desktop app for technicians, and the academy article publishes no browser requirement. Source: infraspeak.com

Worth knowing. The Tuga W10, W8 and WH6 are not recommended as technician devices for Infraspeak. The vendor publishes the Infraspeak Next app for Android and iOS only and publishes no Windows app or browser requirement for technicians, so on a Windows device the work would have to be done through the manager's web interface in a browser, without the offline working, NFC sign-in and in-app scanning the vendor documents for the app. Among the Android devices, the A6 meets the published RAM minimum of 4GB exactly and the A8 runs Android 12 against a recommended Android 13; both meet the minimum, but the A10 is the only Tuga that meets every recommended figure.
Setting up

Getting Infraspeak (Infraspeak Next app) running

  1. Ask your Infraspeak administrator to add the technician as a user, and to assign an NFC tag to the user if you want tag sign-in, which the academy says can be done once per user.
  2. On the Tuga device, open the Google Play Store, search for Infraspeak Next, tap the app and tap Install, as the academy's download article describes.
  3. Open the app, enter the registered email and tap Next, then enter the password and sign in; or hold the device near the user's NFC tag to sign in that way.
  4. Open the app while online and let it synchronise fully before going into areas without signal: the vendor says assets can only be found offline once the app is fully synchronised, and planned job orders must be started while online.
  5. Create a test work order: tap the Plus button, choose Create work order manually, then the building, location, area and type, and tap Create work order; then try the same by scanning a location's QR code or NFC tag.
  6. Walk the worst-signal part of the site with the device, close a work order offline, come back into coverage with the app open and confirm the change syncs, before ordering for the team.

Questions

Infraspeak (Infraspeak Next app) on a Tuga device

Infraspeak publishes a minimum of Android 10, 4GB RAM and 32GB storage, and a recommendation of Android 13, 6GB RAM and 32GB storage, with a camera and NFC sensor for scanning. The Tuga A10 (Android 14, 8GB RAM, 128GB, NFC) meets the recommended figures; the A8 (Android 12, 6GB RAM, 128GB, NFC) meets the minimum and the recommended RAM and storage but not the recommended Android version; the A6 (Android 15, 4GB RAM, 64GB, NFC) meets the minimum with RAM at the floor. We have not tested the app on these devices and do not claim Infraspeak has; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the catalogue, so trial one unit first.

Yes. Every Tuga model lists NFC. Infraspeak's academy says a technician assigns a tag by swiping it near the NFC reader on the mobile device, and that a user can sign in by holding the device near their tag. NFC works over a few centimetres, so the tag has to be placed where the device can reach it; the position of the NFC antenna varies between devices, so find it on a trial unit before you fix tags to plant.

Infraspeak lists Work offline in the app's Google Play description, and its academy explains the rules: actions done offline are stored on the device until the connection returns with the app open, planned job orders must be started while online, and assets can only be found offline once the app is fully synchronised. The detailed list of what works offline is published as an image in the academy article, so check it against your own process. A Tuga A10 or A8 with dual SIM 4G reduces how often you are offline in the first place.

Infraspeak publishes the technician app for Android and iOS only, and describes the manager's features as a web interface and the Infraspeak Manager app. A Tuga W10 can run the manager's web interface in a browser, but Infraspeak publishes no browser requirement and no Windows technician app, so a Windows tablet is not the device to give the people closing work orders.

The Google Play store lists three apps from Infraspeak S.A.: Infraspeak Next for technicians (work orders, scanning, documents, messages, offline working), Infraspeak Manager for managers (the store description names asset management, dashboards and scheduled work), and Infraspeak Operations, described as a mobile interface for anyone who works at a location and needs to check information about it. This page is about Infraspeak Next, the app the device requirements are published for.
